title: Beta-Adrenergic Antagonists
notes: Welcome. Today: how beta-blockers work, who gets them, and why they are not interchangeable.

title: Learning objectives
bullets: Name the beta receptor subtypes and their tissues
Explain the mechanism of beta blockade
List major adverse effects and contraindications
notes: Objectives map to the exam blueprint. Spend most time on selectivity.

title: Mechanism of action
bullets: Net effect: lower cardiac output and blood pressure
notes: Draw the cAMP pathway on the board. Stress that antagonism is competitive, so high catecholamine levels can overcome it.

title: Pharmacokinetics
bullets: Atenolol: renal elimination, t½ about 6-7 h
Therapeutic range often quoted as 50-100 µg/mL for older assays
Lipophilic agents cross the blood-brain barrier
notes: Lipophilicity explains the sleep disturbance and vivid dreams reported with propranolol.

title: Clinical uses
bullets: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

title: Adverse effects
bullets: Bronchospasm in asthma with non-selective agents
notes: Never stop abruptly. Taper over one to two weeks.

title: Interactions to know
bullets: Verapamil or diltiazem: additive AV block

title: Dosing at a glance
notes: Doses are teaching figures only, not a prescribing reference.

title: Case discussion (hidden)
bullets: Which beta-blocker, if any, and why?
notes: Hidden slide: use only if time allows. Expected answer: cardioselective agent at a low dose, with monitoring.

title: Summary
bullets: Competitive beta antagonists reduce cardiac work
Selectivity guides choice, but is dose dependent
